title: Fix a GoPro to a UMI gripper: its two mount fingers between the holder's three, the thumbscrew through all five
instruction: Fix the GoPro to the gripper's holder, lens toward the gripper's fingers: thumbscrew through all five fingers, snug in the nut. Then let go.
context: Handheld grippers such as UMI are how robot-learning labs now gather demonstrations at scale, and each carries an action camera as its only sensor, fixed by the standard GoPro mount: the camera's two folding fingers sit between the holder's three and one thumbscrew runs through all five into a captive M5 nut. The scale is growing fast: over 40,000 demonstrations with such grippers in 32 environments (Lin et al., ICLR 2025) and FastUMI-100K at over 100,000 trajectories, about 600 hours (2025). Every gripper built and every camera swapped is fixed this way. The holes are hidden inside the stack, so the camera is held square in the gaps while the screw's tip finds each hole and the nut, and the screw is turned home, not pushed.
setup: Metres; x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the bench top; origin midway between the arm bases (0, +/-0.305). (1) The UMI handheld gripper, printed from its released files (white top cover and bottom plate, black finger holders, two blue Fin Ray fingers toward -y; body 172 mm long, 91 mm across), held upright at (0.34, 0) by a 30 x 35 mm bar under it in a bench vise: jaws 80 mm wide, tops 65 mm up, the movable jaw at y 20 to 60 mm. On the top cover, the GoPro mount: three fingers 4.0, 3.3 and 4.0 mm thick with 3.3 and 3.4 mm gaps, standing in a row along x, their holes on one line at y 0, 136.4 mm up, from x 0.331 to 0.349; an M5 nut captive in a boss on the far (+x) finger. (2) A GoPro HERO13 Black, model CHDHX-131 (71.8 x 50.8 x 33.6 mm, 159 g with its battery, maker's spec sheet) lying lens up on the bench at (0.21, -0.16), its two mounting fingers folded out toward -y (2.7 mm thick, 15 mm wide, 20.5 mm long). (3) A GoPro-mount thumbscrew with a long knob (Fotodiox GoTough Long, model GT-SCW45: a 45 mm aluminium knob 15 mm across on an 18 mm M5 stainless shaft, 17 g, maker's figures) set down on the vise's movable jaw (where a builder leaves it while fetching the camera, lying clear of the holder; it has no grasp pose on the bench top, so the knob hangs over the edge) along x, shaft toward +x, the knob's end 18 mm out over the jaw's -x edge, at y 0.05. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. The lens must end facing the gripper's fingers (-y). Any camera with GoPro folding fingers serves for a real trial; GoPro's own thumbscrew has a flat paddle that sits under the camera body, where a parallel gripper cannot turn it, hence the long knob.
scoring: Tier numbers are simulation scores; a real trial checks them by close photo (camera fingers in the gaps), ruler photo of the exposed shaft (knob's face no more than about 2 mm short of the first finger, which puts the hidden tip at the nut), light-gap photo (no gap between the knob's face and the first finger; about 2.5 turns in a real nut, 2.0 mm at 0.8 mm a turn) and a paint stripe on the knob (it was turned). A real trial reads every tier at the end of the run. Live tiers, read at the end; the 1.0 is judged once and then holds. 0.25: the camera's two fingers interleaved with the holder's three (within 1.5 mm of the mounted pose along the hole line, 3 mm and 2.5 mm across it, and within 8 degrees of it, lens toward the gripper's fingers). 0.5: and the screw through the stack from the near side: on the holes' line (2 mm), knob's face short of the first finger, tip at the nut's thread (no more than 0.3 mm short). 0.75: and seated by its turns: tip and turned depth within 0.4 mm of the seat, the knob's face on the first finger; depth counts only as turned since the tip reached the nut (0.8 mm a turn, the M5 pitch, plus 0.5 mm of play; the simulated nut seats at about 1.4 turns). 1.0: and each whole gripper (fingers, pads, palm, housing) at least 5 cm from camera and screw, both still, for 1 s. Pushing without turning reaches 0.5 at most. Once seated, camera and screw are fixed where they stand (a tightened screw's friction).
run_limit: 3,200 steps (160 s at 20 Hz); the scripted demo reaches 1.0 at step 2,365 (118.25 s).
reset_notes: Nothing is random. Print the UMI gripper from its open files and clamp it upright in the vise (by a bar under the body) so the holder's hole line runs along x at y 0, 136 mm up, centred at x 0.34. Check the M5 nut sits in its boss. Fold the camera's mounting fingers out and lay it lens up at (0.21, -0.16), fingers toward -y. Unscrew the thumbscrew fully and lay it on the movable jaw along x, shaft toward +x, the knob's end 18 mm over the jaw's -x edge. The reset takes about 2 minutes.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. Real UMI print meshes for the look; collision by a body box, wing hulls and boxes round each hole, so the soft fingers neither collide nor flex. The thread is a rule: once the tip reaches the nut on the holes' line, a joint leaves the screw only its turn (0.15 N m at any turning speed above 3 deg/s) and its slide; depth counts only as turned (0.8 mm a turn plus 0.5 mm play). Sim holes 5.4 to 5.8 mm (real 5.2 to 5.5). Once seated, fixed joints hold camera and screw.
scores: Demo: 1.0 (2,365 steps, 118.25 s; RTX 3090 Ti). push_seat (pushed to the seat) 0.5; no_turn 0.5; light_spin (knob held at 2 N while rolled) 0.5; slow_light_spin (the same, turned at 2 deg/s) 0.5; camera_only 0.25; none 0. Dream-1: 0.0.
failures: Screw pushed in to the seat without turning: 0.5 (depth counts only as turned). Camera set down facing away from the gripper's fingers, or a finger outside its gap: 0 (not interleaved). Screw tip more than 0.3 mm short of the nut's thread, or its axis off the holes' line: 0.25. Seated with a hand still on the camera or the knob: 0.75 until both whole grippers are 5 cm clear and everything is still for 1 s.
